2_proofTest.realSQLiteBoundary: CONFIRMED. Two real temp-file databases per row - `mkdtemp` + `multiplayer-matches.db` (DurableMatchStore) and `mekstation.db` (getSQLiteService, the capability DB the branch port binds on). No jest mocks, no fakes, no in-memory store. The head is read back through `store.readEffectiveHead(streamOf(matchId))` and journal rows counted with raw SQL over `event_journal_events`.
2_proofTest.headProvenanceIsGenuine: CONFIRMED. `seedJournalHead` commits a REAL batch through `store.appendCommandBatch!(...)` - the same boundary the host's commit path calls - and asserts `committed.kind === 'committed'` and `journalCount === 1` BEFORE reading the head. No head row is hand-built. This is the S1-to-S2 join the task owes, and it is exactly what the shipped 14.2 suite (raw-SQL head) could not prove.
2_proofTest.productionDefaultUntouched: CONFIRMED. matchJournalAuthority.ts is NOT in the diff (3-file diffstat re-verified). Read at HEAD: `export const COMBAT_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_MODE = 'off' as CombatJournalAuthorityMode;` (matchJournalAuthority.ts:18-19). The mirror is turned on only by `_setCombatJournalAuthorityModeForTests` (lines 34-38), set in beforeEach and reset to null in afterEach.
2_proofTest.perShapeRefusalAndNoAppend: CONFIRMED for all four. Every shape captures `before = (await store.getEvents(matchId)).length` and `journalBefore = journalCount(matchId)` and asserts BOTH unchanged after the refusal - the match store and the journal, not one of them. Shapes 1/2/4 additionally prove the host survives (shape 1 re-admits after adoptServedBranch; shape 2 receives the same typed refusal on a second intent, where a throw would have killed the match; shapes 3/4 commit the next legal intent).
2_proofTest.absenceAssertionsAreReal: Shape 2 uses `expect(refusal).not.toHaveProperty('conflictHead')` and `.not.toHaveProperty('recoveryAction')` plus `expect(errorOf(frames,'STALE_BRANCH')).toBeUndefined()` - property-absence, not undefined-equality, so a present-but-undefined field would still fail. That is precisely the amended SHALL's 'names no head' half.
2_proofTest.coldReopenIsGenuine: CONFIRMED. `store.close(); resetSQLiteService(); openCampaign(); store = openStore();` then a NEW host - both files closed and reopened from disk. A head living only in an open handle would answer null and admit; the row asserts `readEffectiveHead(...).branchId === CANDIDATE` and then STALE_BRANCH with conflictHead. The disclosed sequence-collision warning on re-persist is real (I observed MATCH_LOG_DIVERGENCE logging in my own run) and is correctly characterised as beside the point - admission answers before the engine.
2_proofTest.modeOffRowIsHonest: CONFIRMED, and it is the honest pin of finding #48: `readEffectiveHead === null`, `journalCount === 0`, no STALE_BRANCH, no MATCH_QUARANTINED, and the intent COMMITS. It does not dress the dead production path as anything else.

4_createPathFinding.citation: ServerMatchHost.create (ServerMatchHost.ts:440-458) builds the host, whose construction-time events go through `persistInitialEvents` (ServerMatchHost.ts:1232-1248, doc comment: 'Persist whatever events the session emitted at construction time (typically GameCreated + GameStarted). Runs as fire-and-forget'), which delegates to the helper calling `await ctx.store.appendEvent(ctx.matchId, evt);` (ServerMatchHostEvents.ts:95). That is the single-event path, NOT `appendCommandBatch` - and appendCommandBatch is the only boundary S1's mirror hooks. The bypass is real as described.
4_createPathFinding.consequenceForS4_task1_4: LOAD-BEARING. Task 1.4 says restart recovery 'rebuilds the live host from the journal head AND the effective branch'. The HEAD survives this bypass (which is why S2 is unaffected), but the journal TAIL does not track the match log once create's non-batch persist runs ahead of the mirror - the author measured the next batch mirroring `revision-conflict`. Any S4 rebuild that reads EVENTS from the journal (rather than only the head) would rebuild an incomplete session. S4 must either seed the mirror at match creation or explicitly restrict itself to head-and-branch reads and say so in its receipt.
4_createPathFinding.consequenceForS6_task1_7: BLOCKING FOR S6, NOT FOR S2. Task 1.7 promises 'shadow parity' and 'new matches admit through the journal'. Shadow parity is structurally unachievable while create's initial events bypass the mirror - the shadow counter starts diverging on the FIRST post-create batch of every match. S6 cannot honestly claim parity until the create path is routed through (or the mirror seeded before) the batch boundary.
4_createPathFinding.isItABlockerForThisSlice: NO. S2's consult reads ONLY `readEffectiveHead` (ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:161-168), and the head is correctly and durably installed by a real mirrored batch - proven live by the cold-reopen row. The suite asserts on the head and explicitly not on the journal tail, and both the test comment and the receipt's nonClaims disclose the gap rather than hiding it. Merging this proof slice does not depend on it.
4_createPathFinding.whereItMustBeClosed: Task 1.7 (S6, the reviewed cutover flag with shadow parity) at the LATEST - that is the box whose promise the gap falsifies. Task 1.4 (S4) is the first consumer that breaks without it and must state its dependency. Recommend S1's disclosed 'no-catch-up' be upgraded from a receipt disclosure to a NAMED remainder on 1.7.
